result.title: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality through Agentic Rule Discovery
result.summary: High-stakes tabular pipelines rely on scattered, static quality checks that are hard to evolve and audit against policy intent. Regulated domains particularly suffer as the LLM-era automation raises expectations for traceability and accountability. We propose a vision for an ontology-grounded, repository-native data quality layer in which rules are first-class artifacts: versioned, provenance-linked to governance texts, and re-playable through immutable execution traces. As a first step toward validating this vision, we present a concrete implementation of its agentic rule-discovery core with two rule acquisition modes (Full-Agentic and Guided) and a human-in-the-loop (HITL) review interface. We define an evaluation framework and run experiments addressing whether our fully autonomous, divide-and-conquer agentic rule discovery produces rules of the same quality and diversity as those specified by a human expert, reporting preliminary results on two real world industry datasets in the finance and retail domains.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出以本体为依托、面向代码仓库的数据质量规则层构想，并实现其智能体式规则发现核心（全自主与引导两种模式，含人审界面），在金融与零售两个工业表格数据集上初步比较自动规则与专家规则的质量与多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为表格数据质量规则的发现、版本与审计，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的 latent 生成、证据使用或训练监督线索，故排除。
